section_summary: This section (March 1934 – September 1936) documents diplomatic correspondence between the Department of State, the War Department, the Federal Communications Commission, the American Embassy in Tokyo, and the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs concerning persistent radio interference. Initial complaints addressed Japanese station interference with U.S. Army transpacific circuits and Japanese vessel transmissions blanketing the 500 kHz international maritime distress frequency. Later correspondence focuses on severe interference caused to RCA coastal station KPH at Bolinas, California, on 8440 kHz by an unidentified Japanese military station signing 'B MW 2'. The Japanese Government consistently defended its operations by asserting earlier registration priority with the Berne Bureau and invoking Article 39 of the 1932 Madrid Convention, leading U.S. officials to consider adjusting American commercial frequencies rather than pursuing further diplomatic protests.

subfiles.about: Requests diplomatic representations to Japan regarding persistent radio interference experienced by Army radio stations, enclosing a summary of incidents.
subfiles.from: Secretary of War George H. Dern
subfiles.summary: Secretary of War Dern requests diplomatic representations to Japan concerning radio interference experienced by Army stations during late 1933, enclosing a summary.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of War George H. Dern to Secretary of State regarding Japanese Radio Interference with Enclosed Summary

subfiles.about: Transmits two copies of the list of radio interference encountered from Japanese stations.
subfiles.from: Major Roger Colton, Signal Corps, War Department
subfiles.summary: Transmits two copies of the list of radio interference encountered from Japanese stations pursuant to telephone conversation.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Major Roger Colton to Eugene H. Dooman regarding List of Interference from Japanese Stations
subfiles.to: Eugene H. Dooman, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Secretary of War's letter of March 5, 1934, and reports instructions were sent to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges the March 5 letter and confirms instructions and interference summaries were sent to the Ambassador at Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State to Secretary of War acknowledging Letter on Radio Interference

subfiles.about: Instructs Ambassador Grew to bring the War Department's report of Japanese radio interference to the attention of the Japanese Government.
subfiles.summary: Transmits War Department letter and summary of interference to Ambassador Grew, instructing him to seek elimination of interference.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 489 from Department of State to Ambassador Joseph C. Grew regarding Army Radio Interference
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmits Federal Radio Commission tabulations of treaty violations by Japanese stations for presentation to the Japanese Government.
subfiles.summary: Encloses FRC tabulations of 1927 Washington Convention violations by Japanese stations, instructing Grew to inform Japanese authorities without urging drastic action.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 491 from Department of State to Ambassador Joseph C. Grew regarding Japanese Violations of Radiotelegraph Regulations
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Reports the Japanese Foreign Minister's explanation that reported radio convention violations were caused by faulty chronometers in the Shipping Bureau.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits Embassy Note No. 203 and Foreign Minister Hirota's reply stating that Japanese ship radio violations were caused by faulty chronometers in the Shipping Bureau.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 851 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew to Secretary of State regarding Japanese Violations of Radiotelegraph Convention Regulations with Enclosures

subfiles.about: Transmits a copy of Tokyo Despatch No. 851 concerning Japanese ship radio violations for the Commission's information.
subfiles.summary: Transmits for FCC information a copy of Tokyo Despatch No. 851 regarding Japanese ship radio violations of Washington Convention regulations.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State to Chairman of Federal Communications Commission transmitting Despatch No. 851

subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese Foreign Office note reporting technical adjustments to eliminate interference from Taihoku stations JFQ and JFA.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Foreign Minister Hirota's note reporting that station JFQ was adjusted to 8600 kHz and JFA equipped with crystals on 12900 kHz, stabilizing frequencies.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 944 from American Embassy Tokyo to Secretary of State regarding Frequency Adjustments for Taihoku Stations JFQ and JFA with Enclosures

subfiles.about: Informs the Secretary of War of Japanese remedial measures on stations JFQ and JFA at Taihoku.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Despatch No. 944 regarding repairs to Taihoku stations JFQ and JFA, noting Tokyo was instructed to pursue remaining interfering stations.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State to Secretary of War regarding Japanese Measures on Stations JFQ and JFA

subfiles.about: Instructs Chargé Neville to make further inquiry regarding the remaining Japanese radio stations causing interference.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Despatch No. 944 and directs the Embassy to inquire further of the Foreign Office regarding other interfering stations reported by War Department.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 605 from Department of State to Chargé Edwin L. Neville regarding Other Japanese Interfering Stations
subfiles.to: Edwin L. Neville, American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmits USCG Haida report of Japanese vessels interfering continuously on the 500 kHz distress frequency and requests representations.
subfiles.from: E. O. Sykes, Chairman, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.summary: Transmits USCG Haida report that Japanese vessels interfere continuously on 500 kHz, ignoring silent periods and distress traffic, and requests diplomatic representations. Includes duplicate.
subfiles.title: Letter from FCC Chairman E. O. Sykes to Secretary of State regarding Interference on 500 kHz Distress Frequency by Japanese Vessels

subfiles.about: Acknowledges FCC letter of October 3, 1934, and reports instructions sent to the Ambassador at Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges receipt of the FCC letter and confirms instructions were sent to Tokyo to seek elimination of the reported 500 kHz interference.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State to Chairman of Federal Communications Commission regarding Japanese 500 kHz Interference

subfiles.about: Instructs Ambassador Grew to make representations to Japan regarding continuous interference by Japanese vessels on the 500 kHz distress band.
subfiles.summary: Quotes USCG Haida report regarding Japanese vessels transmitting continuously on 500 kHz during silent periods, directing Grew to request elimination of the interference.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 661 from Department of State to Ambassador Joseph C. Grew regarding Japanese Vessel Interference on 500 kHz
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmits the Japanese Foreign Office reply and Communications Department report disputing interference claims and shifting blame to U.S. stations.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports Japan's Communications Department either denied causing interference from stations JYB, JAQ, JFH, JFQ, JYC, JYD, and JYT or blamed U.S. stations, while continuing to ignore station JEK. Encloses Note No. 327 and Foreign Office Note No. 134/T2 with technical reply.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1101 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew to Secretary of State regarding Japanese Department of Communications Reply on Radio Interference with Enclosures

subfiles.about: Transmits Tokyo Despatch No. 1101 and notes that Japan failed to address interference from station JEK.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Tokyo Despatch No. 1101 concerning Japanese stations, pointing out that the Japanese Foreign Office made no reference to station JEK.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State to Secretary of War transmitting Despatch No. 1101 on Radio Interference

subfiles.about: Reports that interference has ceased at Hawaii and San Francisco but persists in the Philippines from stations JYB and JFQ.
subfiles.from: George H. Dern, Secretary of War
subfiles.summary: States JEK interference has ceased and mainland traffic is clear, but Philippine traffic suffers severe interference from JYB and JFQ, requesting further representations.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of War George H. Dern to Secretary of State regarding Persistent Radio Interference in the Philippines

subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Secretary of War's letter of June 13, 1935, and confirms instructions were sent to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges the War Department letter regarding Philippine radio interference and confirms instructions were transmitted to the American Embassy at Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State to Secretary of War George H. Dern regarding Action on Philippine Radio Interference
subfiles.to: George H. Dern, Secretary of War

subfiles.about: Instructs Ambassador Grew to convey appreciation for eliminating JEK interference while requesting action against JYB and JFQ.
subfiles.summary: Transmits War Department letter reporting Philippine traffic interruptions by JYB and JFQ, instructing Grew to appreciate JEK's elimination while requesting mitigation of JYB and JFQ.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 782 from Department of State to Ambassador Joseph C. Grew regarding Radio Interference in the Philippines
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmits Embassy Note No. 424 and the Japanese Foreign Minister's reply stating steps were taken to enforce assigned frequencies.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits Embassy Note No. 424 and Foreign Minister Hirota's reply stating that appropriate steps were taken against the concerned wireless stations to maintain rigidly their assigned frequencies.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1472 from Chargé Edwin L. Neville to Secretary of State regarding Japanese Reply on Stations JYB and JFQ with Enclosures

subfiles.about: Transmits a copy of Tokyo Despatch No. 1472 regarding Japanese measures to enforce frequency compliance.
subfiles.from: Francis B. Sayre, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Transmits for the War Department a copy of Despatch No. 1472 from Tokyo reporting Japanese steps to settle the radio interference matter.
subfiles.title: Letter from Assistant Secretary of State Francis B. Sayre to Acting Secretary of War Harry H. Woodring transmitting Despatch No. 1472
subfiles.to: Harry H. Woodring, Acting Secretary of War

subfiles.about: Reports serious interference by Taihoku station JFB to Fort Santiago's reception on 12240 kHz, asserting U.S. registration priority.
subfiles.from: Harry H. Woodring, Acting Secretary of War
subfiles.summary: Reports that Taihoku station JFB severely interferes with Fort Santiago reception from Fort Shafter on 12240 kHz, claiming U.S. registration priority and requesting representations.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of War Harry H. Woodring to Secretary of State regarding Interference by Station JFB at Taihoku

subfiles.about: Instructs Embassy Tokyo to request Japanese cooperation in alleviating station JFB interference as a matter of courtesy.
subfiles.summary: Instructs Embassy Tokyo to inform Japanese authorities that Taihoku station JFB interferes with Fort Santiago reception on 12240 kHz, requesting courtesy assistance.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 170 from Department of State to American Embassy Tokyo regarding Interference from Station JFB

subfiles.about: Clarifies that Japan registered 12240 kHz for JFB before the U.S. Army registered it for WTJ, making any U.S. request a matter of courtesy.
subfiles.from: R. C. de Wolf, Treaty Division, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Explains that War Department's priority claim was erroneous because Japan registered JFB on 12240 kHz in September 1929, before WTJ in February 1930; Lieutenant Pachynski agreed.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum by R. C. de Wolf on Frequency Priority between Station JFB and Station WTJ
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Informs the Acting Secretary of War that Japan holds priority on 12240 kHz, so relief can only be requested as a courtesy.
subfiles.summary: Reports telegraphic instructions sent to Tokyo regarding JFB interference, but clarifies Bern records show Japan registered 12240 kHz prior to WTJ, making relief a courtesy request.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State to Acting Secretary of War regarding Japanese Registration Priority on 12240 kHz
subfiles.to: Acting Secretary of War (Harry H. Woodring)

subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese Foreign Office note promising to install a reflecting apparatus on JFB's antenna and restrict its operation.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew transmits Embassy Note No. 470 and Foreign Minister Hirota's reply stating Japan plans to install a reflecting apparatus on station JFB and minimize its operation on 12240 kHz.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1615 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew to Secretary of State regarding Japanese Plan to Alleviate Station JFB Interference with Enclosures

subfiles.about: Transmits a copy of Tokyo Despatch No. 1615 regarding Japanese measures to alleviate station JFB interference.
subfiles.summary: Transmits for FCC information a copy of Tokyo Despatch No. 1615 and related correspondence concerning Japanese plans to alleviate station JFB interference.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State to Chairman of Federal Communications Commission transmitting Despatch No. 1615

subfiles.about: Transmits Despatch No. 1615 outlining Japanese plans to alleviate station JFB interference and requests reports on future issues.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Tokyo Despatch No. 1615 showing Japanese authorities plan remedial antenna adjustments for station JFB, requesting to be notified if further interference is observed.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State to Secretary of War George H. Dern transmitting Despatch No. 1615
subfiles.to: George H. Dern, Secretary of War

subfiles.about: Reports confidential FCC information that the station interfering with KPH has been established as a Japanese military station.
subfiles.summary: Informs the Far Eastern Division confidentially that the FCC verbally established the station interfering on 8440 kHz is a Japanese military station.
subfiles.title: Confidential State Department Memorandum on Military Character of Interfering Japanese Station
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Transmits RCA complaint and extensive technical data regarding severe interference to station KPH from an unidentified Japanese station on 8440 kHz, requesting a vigorous protest.
subfiles.from: Anning S. Prall, Chairman, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.summary: FCC Chairman Prall requests a vigorous protest to Japan concerning interference to RCA maritime coastal station KPH (Bolinas) on 8440 kHz caused by an unidentified Japanese station signing 'B MW 2'. The filing includes duplicate letter and RCA's submission with station log extracts (Exhibit A), ship complaints from SS Malolo and others, manager reports, direct radiogram communications with Gentel Tokyo (Exhibit B), and monitoring frequency measurements (Exhibit C).
subfiles.title: Letter from FCC Chairman Anning S. Prall to Secretary of State regarding Interference to RCA Station KPH on 8440 kHz with Enclosures

subfiles.about: Acknowledges the FCC letter of July 14, 1936, and reports telegraphic instructions were sent to Tokyo.
subfiles.from: Francis B. Sayre, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges the RCA complaint regarding station KPH and confirms telegraphic instructions were sent to the American Embassy at Tokyo to seek prompt elimination of interference.
subfiles.title: Letter from Assistant Secretary of State Francis B. Sayre to FCC Chairman Anning S. Prall regarding KPH Interference
subfiles.to: Anning S. Prall, Chairman, Federal Communications Commission

subfiles.about: Instructs Embassy Tokyo to make urgent representations regarding interference to RCA station KPH on 8440 kHz.
subfiles.summary: Directs Embassy Tokyo to urge the Japanese Foreign Office to eliminate interference to RCA mobile station KPH (8440 kHz) caused by an unidentified Japanese station signing B MW 2.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 97 from Department of State to American Embassy Tokyo regarding Interference to Station KPH

subfiles.about: Reports the Japanese Foreign Office reply asserting 1928 priority for a military wireless station on 8440 kHz and citing Article 39.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports Foreign Office statement that 8440 kHz was allotted to a Japanese military station in 1928, placing responsibility on the subsequent American station and citing Article 39.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 184 from American Embassy Tokyo to Secretary of State regarding Japanese Claim of Priority on 8440 kHz

subfiles.about: Transmits Tokyo telegram No. 184, analyzes Bern registration records, and suggests exploring a slight frequency change for station KPH.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Embassy Tokyo's report on Japan's military priority claim on 8440 kHz, reviews Bern Bureau registration records showing missing dates in recent lists, and suggests exploring whether RCA can slightly shift KPH's frequency to avoid dispute.
subfiles.title: Confidential Letter from Secretary of State to FCC Chairman Anning S. Prall regarding Japanese Priority Claim on 8440 kHz
subfiles.to: Anning S. Prall, Chairman, Federal Communications Commission

subfiles.about: Discusses strategy for resolving KPH interference by adjusting RCA's frequency to avoid continuing diplomatic discussions with Japan.
subfiles.from: H. B. Otterman, Treaty Division, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Proposes seeking an RCA frequency adjustment in cooperation with FCC to avoid diplomatic controversy, noting that if Japan relinquished the frequency, its Article 39 defense fails.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum by H. B. Otterman regarding Strategy for Settlement of KPH Radio Interference
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Confirms that the FCC and RCA are conducting a further study of the issues involved in the Japanese priority claim on 8440 kHz.
subfiles.from: Anning S. Prall, Chairman, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges the Department's letter of September 21 and states the Commission, in collaboration with RCA, will study the issues further before responding.
subfiles.title: Confidential Letter from FCC Chairman Anning S. Prall to Secretary of State regarding Further Study of KPH Interference

subfiles.about: Transmits the Japanese Foreign Office note asserting 1928 military priority on 8440 kHz and citing Madrid Convention provisions.
subfiles.from: E. R. Dickover, American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits Japanese Foreign Office note arguing that Japan's military station used 8440 kHz continuously since 1928, placing responsibility for interference on subsequent American station KPH, and citing Articles 35 and 39 of the Madrid Convention.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2040 from Chargé E. R. Dickover to Secretary of State regarding Japanese Reply on KPH Interference with Enclosure
